claims.text: A hybrid CE/DFT and AIMD-trained MLIP methodology can accurately predict melting temperatures and entropies of fusion for refractory high-entropy alloys.
Standard CALPHAD methods fail for refractory high-entropy alloys because experimental thermodynamic data are sparse or unavailable at extreme melting temperatures.
Near-equiatomic NbMoTaW can exist as a BCC solid-solution refractory high-entropy alloy.
Near-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is a disordered solid solution characterized by severe local lattice distortion and high configurational entropy.
Severe local lattice distortion is characteristic of the proposed refractory alloy systems.
A cluster-expansion Hamiltonian parameterized with DFT can map solid-state phase stability and order-disorder transition temperatures in these alloys.
An MLIP trained on liquid-phase AIMD trajectories can capture entropy of fusion and liquid-density behavior.
Liquid-density AIMD calculations for HEAs can be conducted at about 1600 °C with a zero-pressure target.
The proposed AIMD regime extends from room temperature to 1600–2000 °C under vacuum.
Severe local lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion and strengthens HEAs.
The liquid structure factor governs entropy of fusion and melting-point depression or elevation.
DFT-parameterized CE bypasses missing experimental thermodynamic parameters by representing the solid-state energy landscape.
AIMD directly represents liquid-state thermodynamics sufficiently to recover melting properties.
Combining constituents with very different melting points can leave undissolved high-melting particles during processing.
Liquid processing of RHEAs can cause segregation of high-melting elements or evaporation of low-melting elements.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the refractory solid solution up to extreme temperatures.
The hybrid model will predict melting temperatures of known RHEAs within 5% of experiment.
Maximizing entropy of fusion will delay melting.
The method is valid when the liquid behaves as a disordered solution and the solid lacks kinetically trapped phase separations that CE cannot capture.
Limited AIMD cell sizes and timescales may miss long-range liquid ordering or rare events that affect entropy of fusion.
